title: EFC Gradient-Coupled Grid Action
description: Presents a minimal three-term Lagrangian for a discrete grid coupled to gravity via a gradient interaction |∇Φ|(∇ξ)². The coupling yields a position-dependent stiffness κ_eff = κ0 + α g and a local dispersion relation that, in the gravitational regime, implies E = ℏω ∝ √g, deriving the EFC screening relation from first principles and establishing operator uniqueness within a defined class.

grid_action.description: Minimal local action for grid displacement ξ with kinetic, bare elastic, and gradient-coupling terms to the gravitational field.

effective_stiffness.description: Position-dependent stiffness induced by the gradient coupling to gravity.

euler_lagrange.description: Equation of motion showing wave propagation with spatially varying stiffness.

dispersion_lattice.description: Lattice dispersion with the standard sinusoidal form and gravity-modulated stiffness.

fundamental_mode.description: Frequency of the fundamental cell mode (k \approx \pi/l_g).

gravitational_regime.description: Gradient-coupling theorem: excitation energy scales with the square root of the local acceleration in the gravitational regime.

crossover.description: Acceleration scale where the transition between bare-elastic and gravitational regimes occurs.

thermal_occupation.description: Bose–Einstein occupation number used to connect dispersion to the macroscopic screening function.

mu_be_form.description: BE-type screening function emerging when E \propto \sqrt{g} with a single acceleration scale a0.

key_results.main_finding: Within a minimal EFT, the unique leading-order local scalar coupling |∇Φ|(∇ξ)² yields κ_eff = κ0 + α g and E ∝ √g in the gravitational regime, providing a first-principles derivation of the EFC screening relation and eliminating alternative operators by symmetry, dimensional, and data-consistency arguments.
datasets_used: Conceptual consistency with SPARC rotation curves (referenced; no new fit performed)

sealed_predictions.statement: Bare stiffness bound: kappa_0 / (alpha a_0) ≪ 1, implying a crossover g_cross = kappa_0/alpha well below a_0 so that the gravitational regime dominates over most galaxy radii.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Global fits of high-quality rotation curves and vertical kinematics that jointly constrain the transition scale; a robust inference g_cross ≳ a_0 (i.e., kappa_0/(alpha a_0) ≳ 1) would falsify this prediction.

sealed_predictions.statement: Sub-kpc dispersion signature: local wave/perturbation speeds follow ω^2(k,g) = [(kappa_0 + alpha g)/m_eff] k^2 (or its lattice form), predicting a √g scaling of phase speed at fixed k in regions where alpha g ≫ kappa_0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Measurements of small-scale fluctuation spectra (e.g., HI/ionized-gas waves, stellar vertical oscillations) across environments with different g showing no √g dependence (or a conflicting g or Φ dependence) at fixed k.

kill_criteria: KC1: Robust, bias-controlled galaxy data demonstrate that the preferred screening form is µ(g) = 1/(exp(g/a0) − 1) (linear g in the exponent) and significantly exclude the √g form across diverse systems at ≥5σ.

KC2: Direct probes of local dispersion (or analogous laboratory/astrophysical wave phenomena) show ω ∝ g (or ω ∝ |Φ| or ρ) rather than ω ∝ √g in regimes where α g ≫ κ0, contradicting the gradient-coupling theorem.

KC3: Clear, reproducible departures from g-only universality: systems matched in local acceleration g but with different density profiles exhibit systematically different µ beyond established scatter, implying dependence on ρ, Φ, or ∇²Φ at leading order.

KC4: Inferred stiffness mapping falsifies κ_eff(x) = κ0 + α g(x): measurements favor zero or opposite-sign correlation between effective stiffness and g, or require leading-order operators other than |∇Φ|(∇ξ)².
KC5: Strong constraints from rotation curves and vertical dynamics yield kappa_0/(alpha a_0) ≥ 1, placing the crossover at or above a0 and removing the gravitational regime where E ∝ √g should hold.
subtitle: Minimal Lagrangian Derivation of E ∝ √g
abstract: Derives the EFC screening relation E ∝ √g from a minimal three-term Lagrangian S_grid. The gradient coupling ½α|∇Φ|(∇ξ)² produces an effective stiffness κ_eff = κ₀ + αg, yielding a local dispersion relation whose gravitational-regime limit recovers E ∝ √g as a theorem. Operator uniqueness is established by systematically eliminating four alternative couplings.

key_equations.grid_action: S_grid = ∫ dt d³x [½m_eff(∂_t ξ)² − ½κ₀(∇ξ)² − ½α|∇Φ|(∇ξ)²]
